verdict.summary: Clio does not review apps before other Clio firms can authorize them. The main requirement is a paid Clio Manage account (any tier except EasyStart) or a 7-day trial to create the app. Composio has no managed app for Clio Manage, so you have to register your own. Review only applies if you want a listing in Clio's App Directory, which includes a security questionnaire and a demo.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for the app itself. A few days of extra work if you want an App Directory listing (security questionnaire, demo video, listing content).
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 15-30 min, if you already have a paid or trial Clio Manage account
verdict.approval_wait: None for authorization by any Clio user. An App Directory listing needs a security review, which Clio says it aims to finish in about 2 business days (2025 source, not specific to Manage), plus the listing steps.

gates.name: Developer application on your own Clio account
gates.unlocks: You can create the app in the Clio Manage developer portal and connect your own Clio Manage account through Composio.
limits: Requires a paid Clio account or a 7-day free trial. EasyStart doesn't support apps.
There's no separate sandbox. Your trial or developer account is the test environment.
Access tokens last 30 days. Refresh tokens don't expire.
Default rate limit is 50 requests/min per access token at peak times, and Clio doesn't raise it on request.

gates.name: Private app (unreviewed) used by other Clio users
gates.unlocks: Other Clio Manage users, in your firm or at client firms, can authorize the same app. Clio doesn't review private apps.
limits: Private apps can't be listed in Clio's App Directory.
The findings found no test-user allowlist and no documented user or install cap.
Each Clio region (US, EU, CA, AU) needs its own Clio account and developer application. Tokens only work in the region that issued them.
After you change scopes, existing users have to re-authorize.

gates.name: Public use, with optional App Directory listing
gates.unlocks: Anyone on a Clio Manage plan that allows apps can authorize the app, with no review required. Optionally, you can be listed in Clio's App Directory and on the App Integrations page via Add to Clio.
limits: Only an App Directory listing requires review: a security and compliance questionnaire, a pre-recorded demo, and onboarding content.
Listed apps must show at least 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis and support current major browsers.
The Certified App Program Silver tier requires at least 100 active Clio customer accounts.
gates.time_to_reach: No wait for unlisted public use. For a listing: security questionnaire (Clio aims for ~2 business days per a 2025 source), then a demo, listing form and draft sign-off.

steps.title: Get a Clio Manage account that allows apps
steps.detail: Start a 7-day free Clio Manage trial, or use a paid Clio account on any tier except EasyStart. Once the trial ends, apply to Clio for a free developer account.
gotchas: EasyStart doesn't support apps, including private apps.
There's no sandbox, so test data lives in this account.
The developer-intake form's approval criteria aren't documented.

steps.title: Sign in to the Clio Manage developer portal
steps.detail: Go to developers.clio.com and sign in with your Clio Manage account, in the region where your users are (for example, US). Use the Clio Manage portal, not the Clio Platform (Grow) one.
gotchas: Clio Manage and Clio Platform apps are separate. A Manage integration needs a Clio Manage client application.

steps.title: Accept the Developer Terms of Service
steps.detail: Clio requires you to accept its Developer Terms of Service before you can build an integration.

steps.title: Create the developer application
steps.detail: Create a new application. Enter a name, your website URL and the redirect URI. Description, icons and a Deauthorization Callback URL are optional; the callback URL receives a notification when a user removes your app.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The redirect_uri in each authorization request has to match a registered redirect URL exactly. Copy it character for character, including https and the path.
The Manage docs describe only the Authorization Code grant. PKCE isn't mentioned.

steps.title: Choose minimal access permissions (scopes)
steps.detail: An agent can work out which Clio resources your tools touch (contacts, matters, activities, calendar entries, bills and so on) and draft the smallest permission set. You then tick those permissions in the application form. If you use the Clio Payments API, include clio_payments.
gotchas: Composio's clio_manage auth config has no default scopes, so choose them explicitly.
If you add scopes later, existing users have to re-authorize.

steps.title: Add the app key and secret to a Composio auth config
steps.detail: Copy the app key (client ID) and secret from the developer portal. In Composio, create an auth config for the clio_manage toolkit using your own credentials, and set the same scopes you selected in Clio.
gotchas: Composio offers no managed OAuth app for clio_manage, so your own credentials are required.
Composio's default authorize and token URLs are Clio's standard (US app.clio.com) endpoints. For EU, CA or AU users, check that the regional URLs match.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection, sign in through Clio's login page, approve the app, and make a simple API call. If you get a 403 ForbiddenError, check whether a scope is missing or whether the user's Clio role is restricting access.
gotchas: If you add a scope in the portal to fix a 403, the user has to re-authorize before it takes effect.

steps.title: Set up separate apps for other regions
steps.detail: If you have users in more than one Clio region (US, EU, CA, AU), create a Clio account and a separate developer application in each region. Each region's app needs its own Composio auth config, because application IDs and tokens only work in their own region.

steps.title: Prepare token handling for other users
steps.detail: Refresh tokens don't expire, so store them encrypted. Treat a 'Token was revoked by the user' error as a reason to ask that user to re-authorize. Optionally, point the Deauthorization Callback URL at an endpoint that cleans up stored connections.

steps.title: Share the app with other Clio users (no review)
steps.detail: Clio doesn't review private apps, and the findings found no documented user or install cap, so you can give the Composio connection link to other Clio Manage users right away. Stop here unless you want an App Directory listing.
gotchas: Private apps can't appear in the App Directory.
Rate limits apply per access token and can't be raised.

steps.title: Optional: request the security review for an App Directory listing
steps.detail: Ask Clio to start the launch process. Clio sends a security and compliance questionnaire (via OneTrust, according to the support guide), and its Application Security and Compliance team reviews your answers. An agent can draft answers about data handling and token storage for you to check.

steps.title: Wait for Clio's security review
steps.detail: A 2025 support article says Clio aims to review submissions within 2 business days. There's no published turnaround specific to Manage.

steps.title: Optional: send the demo and complete the listing
steps.detail: Email a pre-recorded demo to api.partnerships@clio.com. Then fill in the listing form, provide onboarding content, and approve the draft listing before it goes public. For the App Integrations page, add an Add to Clio URL that starts the OAuth flow.
gotchas: Listed apps must show at least 99% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis for core functionality.

requirements.item: Paid Clio Manage account (not EasyStart) or a 7-day trial
requirements.detail: The app key and secret come from a paid or trial Clio account. After the trial, apply for a free developer account.

requirements.item: Accept the Developer Terms of Service
requirements.detail: Required before you can build an integration.
The redirect_uri must match a redirect URL registered in the application settings.

requirements.item: One developer application per Clio region
requirements.detail: US, EU, CA and AU each need their own Clio account and app. Tokens can't be used across regions.

requirements.item: Pass the security and compliance review
requirements.detail: Required only for an App Directory listing. Clio sends a questionnaire and its team reviews your answers.

requirements.item: Pre-recorded demo, onboarding content and listing sign-off
requirements.detail: Email the demo to the API Partnerships team, then complete the listing form and approve the draft listing.

requirements.item: At least 99% uptime and support for current browsers
requirements.detail: Measured on a 30-day rolling basis for core functionality. Applies to App Directory listings.

scopes.scope: Access permissions (contacts, matters, activities, calendar_entries, bills, etc.)
scopes.effect: You select these on the developer application. Request the smallest set you need. Clio doesn't classify any of them as sensitive or as needing extra review. If you change them later, existing users must re-authorize. The scope names come from a third-party guide and haven't been checked against Clio's docs.
Needed for the Clio Payments API. The authenticating user has to accept it during OAuth.

blockers.symptom: You can't create apps, or apps and integrations aren't available on the account
blockers.cause: The Clio account is on EasyStart, or it isn't a paid or trial account
blockers.fix: Start a 7-day Clio Manage trial or move to a paid tier that supports apps, then apply for a developer account.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails with a redirect URI mismatch
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri sent by Composio doesn't exactly match a registered redirect URL
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the application's redirect URIs.

blockers.symptom: Tokens are rejected for EU, CA or AU users
blockers.cause: The tokens were issued by the US endpoint (app.clio.com), or the app belongs to a different region
blockers.fix: Create a developer application in each region, and use that region's authorize, token and API base URLs in a separate Composio auth config.

blockers.cause: A scope is missing on the app, or the user's Clio role doesn't allow the action
blockers.fix: Add the scope in the developer portal and have the user re-authorize, or ask the firm to change the user's role.

blockers.cause: The user removed your app's access in Clio Manage
blockers.fix: Ask the user to reconnect through Composio.

composio.note: Composio doesn't offer a managed OAuth app for clio_manage, so you can't start on managed auth. Register a Clio Manage developer application, paste its key and secret into a clio_manage auth config, and set the scopes yourself because the default list is empty. Composio's default endpoints are Clio's standard (US) authorize and token URLs; for other regions you need a separate app and matching regional URLs.

open_questions: Is there an install, user or distribution cap on unreviewed private Clio Manage apps? None was found in the docs or changelog.
What are the exact Manage scope names, and are any of them sensitive or restricted? Clio's permissions page relies on a UI screenshot, and the example names come from a third-party guide.
How long does a Manage App Directory review take? The only figure is a 2-business-day target from a 2025 support article about public apps in general.
What are the approval criteria for a free developer account after the trial? The developer intake page couldn't be read.
Does Manage support PKCE or refresh-token rotation? The Manage authorization docs don't mention either.
Does Composio's clio_manage auth config let you change the authorize, token and API URLs for EU, CA or AU apps?
Has the Add to Clio and App Integrations listing flow changed since the 2025 snapshots?
